source: (No manners at all. What an imp.)
What was that, Laertes?
Nothing, my lord. The stew tonight is excellent.
The quality is not in its appearance, but its taste, my lord.
Well, Mother's dinner has been well plated. Only mine looks like it's been stirred up.
Here. If it truly bothers you so, I'm more than happy to switch.
No, no, my lady—
If the food does not please your majesty, I will return it to the kitchen at once!
No need, Irma. Truly.
See? Delicious.
Oh, goodness.
Er, I feel suddenly ill. I'm going to be sick here, I fear. Can someone--
Can someone help me to--
What in God's name—?
Her mouth— blood--
What was she fed? Who put such a thing in her meal?
Seize Irma immediately!
Uncle. Your mouth.
I don't feel right, either.
You've got blood on your lips.
Poison. Poison?
Men, t-to me, at once! Urgh--
She killed them both.
N-no! My lady, I meant-- I intended--
She was trying to murder me.
What is happening? Why?
You idiot child! I meant it to be you!
Guards, take her at once. Let her rot in the cell until I decide what to do with her.
You treat me as if I am a child.
In the scheme of things, you are.
I detest you utterly. You know that, don't you?
That's the strange thing about motherhood, darling. You may despise me more than anything in the world, but I will love you ever still.
No amount of anger or rejected dinners can take that love from me.
So it would seem.
Everyone, please, a moment.
I... felt it appropriate to address the room tonight, in light of everything that's happened.
My lord?
It's all right, Bernardo. Really.
I wanted to disclose the identity of my uncle's killer.
I'm certain many of you are wondering about the circumstances under which he died.
Let there be no more secrets between us. I killed him.
Hmm. Bold. I like it.
Oh, Hamlet...
Allow me to tell you all why.
Before Claudius wore the crown, he poured poison into my father's ear as he slept.
That poison killed my father instantly, and left my mother and I bereft.
Claudius did this knowing the pain it would cause my mother, and the instability it would cause our country.
He did it for the sake of his own petty greed.
I saw an opportunity to seek vengeance for my father's death, and I took it.
That is all. No more, no less.
Please, excuse me.
Leave her be. I'll speak to her when I can.
Please, all of you, take great care with my mother during this time.
For what little made him good, Claudius loved my mother a great deal.
And what makes you fit to be King, Hamlet?
You've been a blubbering mess of a fool these last few months. We all saw it.
Now you're going to stumble your way into the throne of Denmark?
Failure should be its own reward.
I, for one, would support the nobility voting on another candidate entirely.
You've never failed to make your preferences known, Laertes, have you?
And of course, your first preference has always been that I would curl up and die.
I'm not going to do that. I'm here to rule.
So if you'd like to express concerns with my claim to the throne, do so in whatever way you deem fit.
It won't matter.
My lords and ladies: Eat up, for your health. Please.
It all tastes like ash.
Is something wrong, my dear?
How did things become like this?
You know you aren't to blame.
If my son's gone away where I can never see him again, how can that be what's best for him?
He's so young, Claudius.
Does he even understand what he did? Will anyone be there to guide him? To comfort him?
The thought of him being frightened and cloudy, alone, in England-- it's too much for me.
I can't bear the thought of my poor son like this.
I promise you, this journey is exactly what the boy needs.
Dearest, please. You mustn't give into the dark.
Be strong for your country. Be strong for me.
(Besides, the wretched boy will be back soon enough.)
It doesn't matter.
I wish God had taken me, too.
Dearest, please. You mustn't give into the dark like this.
Be strong for your country. Be strong for me. Even if Hamlet's gone, I need you. You see that, don't you?
Right now, I see nothing.
Hamlet won't even attend his supper.
The boy's simply being his usual surly self. He'll come round.
And if he doesn't? What then?
Then we shall address it—together.
Please excuse me. I have no appetite.
The sun has long gone down. Father will be after me if I'm not in my rooms.
Something's different. The book on the table's not where I left it.
Is someone in here?
T-the door—
N-no, I'm sure it's nothing...
I really ought to get some sleep.
My head won't stop throbbing.
It feels as if something's--
Oh, dear. This won't do.
Thank goodness.
Father? What happened?
You had a fainting spell. You've been asleep.
We're fortunate someone saw you collapse and raised the alarm.
Ah, some traveling thespian. Peter Quince, his name was, I think. Here to perform a play for His Majesty.
Ophelia, you must be more careful. I've called for the court physician, but I don't know how soon he'll be here.
If something worse had happened, I--
Father, I'm all right. I feel perfectly fine now.
And how wonderfully grateful I am for that.
If you see that Quince man, you must thank him profusely.
I believe he's putting on a performance in just a few minutes in the Great Hall. If you dress and go now, you'll make the start of it.
That would be an opportune time to express your gratitude, don't you think?
I've got to attend to His Majesty--but please don't overtax yourself. I beg of you.
The performance is about to start.
I wonder if that's the man my father mentioned.
So terribly good to see you in the land of the living.
I must express my most sincere thanks to you, Sir Quince.
Please, no 'sir'. Peter Quince, the one-man thespian. At your service anytime, my lady.
I'm passing through to put on one of my performances for His Majesty's court.
When I saw you collapse earlier, you gave me quite a start!
Were it not for you, I'm not certain what would have happened.
It is rather disarming when one's mortal coil fails one, isn't it?
Indeed. On that topic, have you been to Elsinore before? We've had performers at the castle often, but I cannot say I recall your face.
I've visited now and then over the years. It is unfortunate I have never made your acquaintance. Coincidence, perhaps. Or fate!
Now please, you must excuse me. My performance is about to begin, after all.
But if you ever find you need assistance in your endeavors, please do find me.
And what 'endeavors' might those be?
That's neither here nor there. Suffice to say, there are fascinating things at work in Elsinore Castle.
The machine which has been set in motion can no longer be halted. Not now.
It will be frightening at first. But then everything will become clear.
And then we shall speak further, you and I.
Hmm. He's not here. Strange.
It's the middle of the night. I tried to stay asleep. I really did. But I just couldn't.
Not after what I saw.
S-So King Claudius is a murderer. And no one but Hamlet and I know.
There were whispers he'd killed his brother after King Hamlet's sudden death. But... nothing with substance.
Hamlet must have worked with Quince to put on a performance he thought would get Claudius to confess.
But he didn't kill Claudius when he heard his confession, though I feared he might.
Come to think of it, Claudius might come after us now, too.
I don't know what will happen tomorrow. I'm afraid. What if things get worse?
Ah. Found you. What brings you here?
Have you seen Father?
Ophelia, something unfortunate has happened.
What is it?
Ah. Found you. It's early for you to be wandering out like this.
I couldn't sleep. Do you need something?
Something unfortunate has happened.
Ah. You're awake. I thought you might be asleep.
I'm deeply sorry to be the one to tell you this.
Your father has passed away. He was involved in an altercation with Prince Hamlet.
W-what? Father?
How? You're saying Hamlet killed Father?
Hamlet wasn't in his right mind, Ophelia. He was... raving, insane. I've never seen him like that.
I'm so sorry. It happened in the Queen's private chambers last night. I wasn't there to save him.
Why was my father in the Queen's chambers? How did all of it come to pass?
At this time, my lady, I have no information.
Apologies to have come to you like this, so abruptly. I felt certain you'd want to know.
Please take me to see him.
Er—we have not been able to find the body, as of yet.
Hamlet has gone and hidden it somewhere. My men are searching as we speak.
I think Hamlet himself is undergoing a complete break from reality, of sorts.
Your father was a good man. This was a horrible tragedy. Nothing you might have done would have prevented this.
That's not true. I saw it. I saw him die by Hamlet's hand in my dream, Bernardo.
And I did nothing!
I could've saved him. But I thought it was only a dream!
Ophelia, it was just a dream. Dreams aren't reality. Whatever vision you saw, it was just that.
All this-- I feel like I'm going mad.
What am I to do now, Bernardo?
I just want to be with Laertes. I need my brother.
I know, Ophelia. I know.
I'll do my absolute best to bring Laertes back to Elsinore as soon as possible.
And... for what little it's worth, I am deeply, truly sorry.
You and I have both known Hamlet all our lives. Never did we think him capable of murder.
At the end of the day I am the one wearing the armor. It was my duty to protect your father, and I failed him.
Come. I have to break the news to the rest of the castle.
My lord, I understand there is the matter of a missing lute from many years ago to attend to.
You mean Laertes' lute. Did Ophelia send you after me?
Indeed, my lord.
I imagine he's holding quite the grudge over it.
Can we drop the titles just for a minute, Bernardo? We're talking about a time when we used to dare each other to eat mud.
The dog thinks I stole it from him. I didn't, right? You remember, don't you?
Of course I do. He lent it to me, though he doesn't remember, of course. Laertes always was quick to blame you.
Well, the solution to the matter is simple. If he lent it to you, just give his lute back.
Err, w-well...
